scope.flow: PrecompileReader.suppliedBalance() reads 0x811 supplied balance, MonetrixAccountant._readL1Backing() accumulates it into totalBackingSigned(), and settle() distributes inflated surplus as yield
scope.environment: Hyperliquid PM-enabled protocol with 0x811 precompile, MonetrixAccountant, Vault, YieldEscrow, Operator settlement
evidence: PrecompileReader.suppliedBalance() discards 0x811 borrow liabilities, causing each settlement cycle to silently extract real USDC as phantom yield after PM is enabled, cumulatively eroding protocol solvency

Hyperliquid's 0x811 precompile (PRECOMPILE_SUPPLIED_BALANCE) returns the full BorrowLendUserTokenState struct containing four uint64 fields: borrow.basis, borrow.value, supply.basis, supply.value. PrecompileReader.suppliedBalance() only extracts the fourth field (supply.value) when decoding, completely discarding the borrow information in the first two fields.

MonetrixAccountant._readL1Backing() iterates over all registered SuppliedAssets, accumulating supply values into total via suppliedUsdcEvm() or suppliedNotionalUsdcFromPerp(), without ever subtracting borrow values at any point.

PM is a fully planned and implemented feature path in the protocol, not a hypothetical scenario. The contracts contain setPmEnabled(), notifyVaultSupply(), PM branches in _sendL1Bridge(), and the entire 0x811 read pipeline, all specifically written for PM mode. Governor enabling PM via setPmEnabled(true) is an expected governance operation. Once PM is enabled, the Vault automatically registers 0x811 supplied slots in the Accountant when executing hedges and BLP operations, through executeHedge() and supplyToBlp().

After PM is enabled, auto-borrow requires no attacker to trigger. The Hyperliquid PM engine automatically manages the Vault's L1 account borrowing based on market conditions (funding rate changes, collateral value fluctuations, margin requirement adjustments). This is a core PM mechanism, not an edge case. The Vault contract only has sendSupply (op=0) and sendWithdrawSupply (op=1) operations, with no explicit borrow operation, suggesting the protocol developers may not have anticipated that PM would produce borrow liabilities, which explains why PrecompileReader completely ignores the borrow fields.

totalBackingSigned() is therefore permanently inflated: suppose the Vault supplies 500,000 USDC and 200,000 USDC is auto-borrowed, the net value should be 300,000 USDC, but the Accountant counts the full 500,000 USDC. surplus() and distributableSurplus() inherit this inflated value. When the Operator calls settle(proposedYield) as part of normal duties, Gate 3 checks proposedYield <= distributableSurplus(). Because distributableSurplus includes 200,000 USDC of phantom surplus, Gate 3 does not block this yield distribution that should not have passed. settle() then transfers real EVM USDC into YieldEscrow, and the Operator distributes it via distributeYield() to sUSDM holders, InsuranceFund,

This loss automatically repeats every settlement cycle without any human intervention. Gate 4's annualized APR cap (default 1200bps = 12%) only limits the extraction rate per settlement, it does not prevent cumulative losses. With 10M USDM supply, each 21-hour settlement cycle extracts approximately 6,904 USDC of phantom yield. Over 30 days across approximately 34 settlement cycles, this accumulates to roughly 234,000 USDC of real funds extracted. If the borrow persists or grows, the protocol will trend toward insolvency (backing < totalSupply) within months, violating the INV-1 solvency invariant.
